findings.reason: an orphaned section is never built; it needs an edge and a queued invocation (and §26, which makes the store the only store, is the natural successor to depend on it).
findings.text: §29 is declared implementable yet sits in no dependency edge and in no followup: `plan-section-depends-on` lists only s26 and s27, and `f-hpdw-011` (plan.html:468) queues §24 and §28, then §26 and §27, so no dispatch will ever name §29 and the store reader that §24 and §26 have already made load-bearing keeps turning a damaged file or a pre-`payload` schema into an empty population

findings.reason: a clause that cannot fail makes the section's "each failing at the base revision" unachievable as written, and the author must either scope red-first to the two failure arms or restate the equality over a shape the readers currently disagree on.
findings.text: §29 requires "the ledger reader and the indexed reader return the same rows over the same store" as one of its new tests, "each failing at the base revision", but measured at base over a two-row single-project store both readers return identical records (`stored_run_rows` ids `['run-a','run-b']`, `_indexed_records` ids `['run-a','run-b']`, equality True), so that clause's test passes on the unfixed code and a worker must either fabricate a red or drop the clause

findings.reason: the section's endpoint, an error naming the store and the cause, is right for all three arms and each is still testable; only the Why's account of what the attach arm produces would need a word.
findings.text: §29's Why says the reader's `except sqlite3.Error: continue` turns "a damaged file, a failed attach or a mismatched schema into an empty population"; in `reckon/run_store.py` the attach failure is swallowed separately (`except (OSError, sqlite3.Error): pass`) and the read continues against `main`, so a failed attach loses archive rows only, and the query guard is a `break` out of a batch loop rather than a per-table `continue`
